person_made_it: Eric is the maker: the canvas is his own Dragon House emblem (teal oval, white dragon-prow, gold rim, redrawn in vector), and the keepsake says Painted by Eric, Stoughton, Wisconsin.
emcee_who_is_speaking: Darby speaks only in short labels and the verified Rogaland line; the brush, the fiddle and Eric's own strokes do the talking.
what_time_of_day_is_this_room: Morning light on a pine painter's bench, the hour a rosemaler sits down with fresh paint.
did_the_click_pay_me: Every stroke grows into scrolls, leaves or tulips with liner commas, mirrored 2 or 4 ways, and rings a Hardanger fiddle note; Bloom finishes the piece and it frames itself; a single tap also paints.
works_for_the_recipient: Phone: sticky canvas with touch, 48px tools, 1800px keepsake. PC: three-column layout, larger canvas at native DPR, hover brush ring with mirror ghosts, keyboard shortcuts with on-screen keys, fullscreen, 3200px PNG export. Tested to the keepsake in WebKit 390, Chromium 1920 and 2560.
taught_me_something: Stoughton is a center of the symmetrical Rogaland style (UW-Madison folklife), which is why the mirror brush is the right tool, and the town hosts the largest Syttende Mai celebration in the United States.
told_me_the_truth: Facts are sourced in PROVENANCE: Stoughton Chamber, UW folklife, Wikipedia via Milwaukee Magazine. The dragon is a redrawing, not his original file, and is labeled as code-drawn.
weakest: The generative strokes are good folk-art shorthand but not a master's hand: acanthus can read feathery when dragged fast, and the vector dragon is a simplified cousin of Eric's emblem rather than an exact match.
